transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Hello! How are you feeling after your cataract surgery? Do you have any questions about your recovery or surgery?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Hi! I'm doing okay, thank you. Yes, I do have a few questions. First, when can I start doing a little bit of gardening?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: After cataract surgery, it's recommended to avoid strenuous exercise, lifting heavy objects, and activities that might strain your eyes or increase your heart rate for about a month. However, light exercise like brisk walking, gardening, and gentle cycling can be resumed after 1 week. Just remember to take it easy and not overexert yourself. If you have any concerns, it's always best to check with your care team. Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Thank you for that information. I also wanted to ask, when can I start using my eye gel for dry eyes?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: You should continue to use your eye drops as prescribed. If you're running out, your GP should be able to provide some more. It's also mentioned in the information that preservative-free eye drops can help with dryness, so you can try getting some of those from the pharmacist and using them four times daily to start.

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Great, thank you. Another thing I've been noticing is that I'm very sensitive to bright light. Is that normal?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.intended: Some sensitivity to light is normal as your eyes adjust to the new lenses. If it's mild, you can try wearing sunglasses when you're going outside. However, if it's severe or accompanied by pain, redness, or discomfort, we may need to assess it further. Does that make sense? Do you have any other questions?
